q: Simplify: $$\dfrac{[5\operatorname{cis}(65^\circ)][6\operatorname{cis}(15^\circ)]}{2\operatorname{cis}(20^\circ)}.$$ Express your answer in the form $a+bi$.
The points $P$ and $Q$ have polar coordinates $\left(2,\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ and $\left(4,\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$. Find the distance between $P$ and $Q$.
Solve for $z$: $$(z-1)^2=8-8\sqrt{3}i.$$ Express your answer in the form $a+bi$.
Change from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates: $\left(4,\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$
Express $$\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2}i\right)^5}{\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}i\right)^8}$$ in $r\operatorname{cis}\theta$ form where $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<\pi$.
If $20\operatorname{cis}\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)$ is a fourth root of $5z$, find $z$. Express your answer in the form $a+bi$.
Simplify: $$\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}i\right)^{2021}.$$ Express your answer in the form $a+bi$.
The polar equation $$r=\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2\sin\left(\theta-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}$$ can be written as a rectangular equation of the form $y=ax+b$. Find $a+b$.
Solve for $z$: $$z^3=\dfrac{\left(2\operatorname{cis}\dfrac{5\pi}{12}\right)^4}{-\sqrt{3}-i}.$$ Express your answer in the form $a+bi$.

The curve whose graph is shown has a polar equation of the form $r=a+b\sin\theta$ such that $a$ and $b$ are real numbers and $0\le\theta<2\pi$. The curve passes through the points $C(-3,0)$, $D\left(-9,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, and $E\left(3,\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$. Find the values of $a$ and $b$.
The vertices of $\triangle BVF$ have polar coordinates $B(6,-15^\circ)$, $V(0,90^\circ)$, and $F(-8,45^\circ)$. Find the perimeter of $\triangle BVF$.
If $z_1=2\operatorname{cis}\dfrac{7\pi}{10}$ is a 6th root of $z_2$, find the cube roots of $z_2$. Write your answer in the form $r\operatorname{cis}\theta$, where $0\le\theta<2\pi$.
A point has Cartesian coordinates $\left(-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{6}\right)$. Find the polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ of this point if $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<2\pi$.
Transform the polar equation $$r=\dfrac{3}{6+5\cos\theta}$$ into an algebraic equation of the form $Ax^2+Bxy+Cy^2+Dx+Ey+F=0$.
Given $z=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}i$, find $z^0+z^3+z^6+z^9+z^{12}+\dots+z^{99}$. Express your answer in the form $a+bi$.
The point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-2,-2)$. Find the polar coordinates of $P$ with $r>0$ and $0<\theta<2\pi$.
Find all of the fourth roots of $4-4i\sqrt{3}$. Express your answer in $r\operatorname{cis}\theta$ form, where $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<2\pi$.

Rewrite the polar equation $$\dfrac{r}{\sin\theta}=\dfrac{5}{1-3\sin 2\theta}$$ as an algebraic equation in the form $Ax^2+Bxy+Cy^2+Dx+Ey+F=0$, where the non-zero values of $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$, and $F$ are relatively prime integers.
Change from rectangular coordinates to polar coordinates: $\left(-6,6\sqrt{3}\right)$ if $0<\theta<2\pi$ and $r>0$.
Transform the Cartesian equation $4x^2-y^2=4$ to a polar equation. Express $r^2$ in terms of $\cos\theta$.
Evaluate $$\left(4\operatorname{cis}(15^\circ)\right)^3\left(2\operatorname{cis}(30^\circ)\right)^2.$$ Write your answer in the form $a+bi$.
$z=\sqrt{6}\left(\operatorname{cis}\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)$. Write $z$ in $a+bi$ form.
Transform the polar equation $$r=\dfrac{4}{2-\sin\theta}$$ into an algebraic equation of the form $Ax^2+Bxy+Cy^2+Dx+Ey+F=0$.
Given points $A$ and $B$ with polar coordinates $\left(-2,-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ and $\left(6,\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)$. Find the distance between points $A$ and $B$.
Evaluate: $$\left[3\operatorname{cis}\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right]^3\left[2\operatorname{cis}\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right]^2.$$ Write your answer in the form $a+bi$.
The graph of the polar equation $\cot\theta-2\tan\theta=1$ consists of two lines. Find the algebraic equations of the two lines in the form $y=mx+b$ where $m$ and $b$ are real numbers.

Compute $$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)^1+\left(\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)^3+\dots+\left(\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)^{2013}.$$ Write your answer in the form $a+bi$.
If $w=(2\operatorname{cis}105^\circ)\cdot(3\operatorname{cis}108^\circ)\cdot(1\operatorname{cis}27^\circ)$, rewrite $w$ in $a+bi$ form.
If $$z=\dfrac{(4i)^{5/2}}{\left(1-i\sqrt{3}\right)^3},$$ rewrite $z$ in $r\operatorname{cis}\theta$ form, where $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<2\pi$.
Find all complex number solutions of $x^4-8-8i\sqrt{3}=0$. Leave answers in polar form where $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<2\pi$.
